text: Australia has a growing health problem and it's slowly hurting us.
And the source of this problem is hiding in the foods we eat every day.
It's salt.
We're consuming almost double the recommended maximum daily salt intake of 5 grams,
without realising how much damage it's doing to our health.
Ever wondered why this is a problem?
Salt is made up of sodium and chloride,
and it's sodium that in large quantities can be bad for your health.
Too much sodium in your blood causes fluid overload,
which over time can lead to high blood pressure,
and this can damage your arteries.
This means less blood can get to your organs,
like your heart, brain and kidneys.
If blood can't get to your heart, you could have a heart attack.
If blood can't get to your brain, you could have a stroke.
And high blood pressure could cause stress on your kidneys,
leading to kidney disease.
One in three Australians has high blood pressure.
Your food choices today affect your health tomorrow.
You may not feel it now, but once your organs are damaged,
it's often irreversible.
To protect you and your family from the dangers of salt,
eat fresh food and reduce processed and packaged food.
Read the label and look for less than 400 milligrams of sodium per 100 grams.
To find out more, visit unpackthesalt.com.au
